title: Charges rejected in custody death
article: Charges will not be laid in the death of a Prince George man who was wrestled down and tasered by city RCMP, a prosecutor said Thursday.

Regional Crown counsel Oleh Kuzma said none of the officers involved in Clay Willey's arrest last July has been implicated in his death -- an accusation levelled at police by the man's family. Kuzma said he made the decision this week but wouldn't say why he came to that conclusion. "In view of the coroner's inquest that will be taking place, I'm not going to discuss the matter any further," he said. In cases involving allegations against police, he said a decision on charges is made jointly by the regional prosecutor and Crown counsel at Vancouver headquarters. A coroner's inquest must also be held whenever someone dies in police custody, but a date has not been set.

An earlier investigation by North District RCMP, which oversees detachments in northern B.C., cleared police of any criminal wrongdoing. But Kuzma had sent the case back for further investigation in November. "I got the information I required and the decision was made after that," he said.

RCMP Supt. Dahl Chambers said he's confident in the quality of the investigation by North District RCMP and the independent review by Crown counsel. "I now look forward to the coroner's inquest where all activities by all parties can be fully disclosed for the public's full information," he said.

Bryna Willey, the dead man's sister, said she's not satisfied and won't give up her fight to find out what happened to her brother. "I'm a little disappointed in the system, but we still have the coroner's inquest to go through, so maybe we'll see justice there," she said. Willey's family had hired a lawyer to collect additional information from witnesses, which she said was forwarded to Crown counsel.

She said Willey's family and friends are gearing up for another round of demonstrations at the courthouse, protesting police treatment. In the weeks following Willey's death, his supporters rallied outside the RCMP detachment and the courthouse.

Willey, 33, died in hospital July 22, 16 hours after he was initially arrested in the parking lot of Parkwood Place mall for allegedly causing a disturbance. RCMP said he was aggressive and irrational throughout the arrest and was zapped three times with an electric taser gun in an attempt to subdue him. He had to be resuscitated in the ambulance en route to the hospital, where he died 16 hours later.
